title: S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson OTA Press Conference  | Arizona Cardinals 2026
text: I got the sniffles, so y'all excuse me if I sniff. Yeah. >> So, do you feel like a veteran? >> Um no, not really. I feel like every day I come in here, I'm still learning. Um you know, I'm going into my third year, but I treat it just like I just got here, you know. So, uh I wouldn't say that you can consider me a vet, but I still feel like I just I'm fresh here and still learning, so. >> Rab, after Dewey got here, he said you were one of the first people to reach out to him. Why was it important for you to reach out to him? >> So, uh you know, I'm a I'm a ball guy. I like all the guys in the league, you know. So, uh I actually followed him on Instagram cuz I found out we were in the same agency. You know, his agent and my agent are really good buddies. So, I followed him on Instagram, and then literally 2 weeks later, my agent called me. He was like, "Hey, Dewey might come out to Arizona." So, I followed him on Instagram, and out of nowhere, he just shows up. So, I texted him uh I'm like, "Hey, bro, I got my a lot of respect for you, you know, excited for you to be out here with the team." So, uh he's one of those guys that, you know, you you you you play ball around the league, you know, you watch everybody's game, you try to develop a little bit of that. Uh super smart guy, super super smart guy. So, I'm glad he's on our team now. >> What is it like in that in that safety room now? I mean, obviously, Buddha's still there, and Buddha's Buddha, but but JT had been here a long time, and um just in terms of like is the vibe a lot different now, or >> No, um I mean, you would think that, but you know, um it's kind of just like how you got all you guys hang around. When someone new comes around, you guys welcome him with open arms, and nothing really changes. So, you know, uh you know, just a little bit of verbage change, um but other than that, man, you know, new guys come in, you welcome them in, you know, we all got the same goal, and that's to win here. So, you know, we bring those guys in, uh introduce them to the culture in the room, you know, our standards in our secondary room. So, yeah, I wouldn't say it's too much of a change at all, but we do miss JT. Yeah, he had a little He he definitely brought uh some smiles and laughters to the room, but so does a lot of other guys in the room as well. >> You You some of the verbage is Buddha was talking a little bit about how this is the most he's seen Nick Rolovich change things up from one off-season to the next. I guess from your perspective, is or is that also true from your perspective and how much have things changed this year? >> Yeah, you know, took some It's the same thing you go through every single year, you know, you're going through the year. For those guys, they evaluate everything and we evaluate our game. You take something out, add something in. You simplify one thing and you simplify another thing. So, you know, there's a there are some things different, you know, our defense is still defense like X's and O's are X's and O's, you know, cover one's cover one, cover one's cover cover two's cover two and cover three's cover three, you know, so nothing nothing really changes as well, you know, we got coaches that have left here, you know, so obviously, you know, a little of the verbage changed cuz we got to play against some of those guys this year, but other than that, man, it's really it's really all the all the same, you know, you know, shrink it down, make it more, you know, simplify, more complex for us to go out there and just run around with our hair on fire. >> How beneficial can it be to have Rolovich sticking around? >> Me, personally, you know, I like it, you know, coming in my third year, you know, just trying to make my game and improve every single year. Don't got to learn anything new. So, at this point in my in my career right now, I'm just sharpening all my tools, you know, I really I don't take it the wrong way, but I really don't care who the coach is, you know, I'm coming in to play my game every single day regardless of who's in the building and who's out the building. So, you know, I look at it as a plus that he's here, you know, but I come in the building every day and I perfect my craft at the end of the day. >> I guess after what you just said, I don't know if this will be important to you, but uh have you had a chance to interact with Coach Austin much at all and if you have, uh what's that been like? >> Coach Austin, my bad. >> Terrell Austin. Terrell Austin. >> Oh, my bad, yeah, lot of new guys, yeah, I probably I I probably know nicknames, yeah, so but all the coaches in the building You talking about TA? There you go. You should have My bad, you yeah, I was like, hold on. I was like, I know nicknames around the building. No, TA is cool. Um he's one of those guys when I come in, you know, always yo, TA make sure, you know, make sure he's in the building and he always joke around, but he's one of those guys that he walks around and he's in the background in the shadows. You know, he knows a lot of ball, knows a lot of ball. So any chance I can get to go sit down with lunch at him, you know, and just talk 5 minutes, 10 minutes or either on the sideline after rag, it's like, hey, what do you see here? What did I do wrong? And he gives me, you know, those nuggets that I can uh improve in my game. >> Sorry about that. >> Now, you threw me for a curveball. That was like, hold on, hold on. >> [laughter] >> TA, no, yeah. >> You talked a little bit about JT being down. Like, I I guess going into last year, you knew right Bud and JT were there and and you're competing for different types of snaps. Whereas now, you're competing for for one of those starting full-time jobs. Does anything change for you kind of in that role when when you're you have a different opportunity in front of you? >> Um I guess you could say that a little bit. You know, those two guys, they helped me a lot in my game coming in. You know, I see both of those guys as mentors. I was more in the boundary than I was in the field. So I was I spent a lot of time with JT. I learned a lot from him. You know, I owe, you know, a little bit of credit to my success to him and Bud as well. Also, the other guys in the room. So going into those two years with them, you know, was amazing, but now I'm going into my own year, you know, he's gone. I mean, can't can't do anything about that. So you know, like I said earlier, I come in the building every single day and put one foot in front of the other, man. Then, you know, the day ends, I go home. I correct what needs to be corrected and at the end of the day, we come in and who we have on our team is who we have on our team. >> Looking back after last season ended and evaluating your play up until this point in the offseason, what have been your main focuses in your game to step it up? >> Uh for me personally, you know, there's a lot of guys that have experience on this team. I want to understand X's and O's and know a lot better, you know, I'm not saying I'm a dumb football player because I knew I do know ball and and I can ball, but just understanding the game a lot more, you know what I'm saying? So, and that just comes with experience in this league, you know, you got guys in our room that have played 5, 6 years, Buddha 10 years. So, you know, there's They know some things that I don't and I know some things that they don't. So, you know, just going in that room and when we're talking ideas just bounce off the wall left and right, man. And that's what I That's what I love about our room. We're always communicating. It's kind of like a DB thing. We just talk a lot. So, yeah, that room really helps me come into come to work every day. >> How can you speed that up besides years and things? >> Say that again? >> How can you speed up learning more and kind of figuring out the >> Oh, it just takes reps, man, you know, It just takes reps and repetition and seeing different things, you know, we got a new offense now. So, just learning our offense, you know, we're not really game planning against anybody now, but it is different, you see what I'm saying? And I like that we have offensive minded head coach, so we get that cross training and that's one thing I like with the hiring of Mike. >> What are your early impressions of this offense? >> Early impressions of this offense? They do a lot moving around, you know, we're seeing a bunch of stuff that you usually won't see until the season or going into a game plan. So, it's nice. I feel like we're going to be very prepared going into week one. >> Asante did >> Go ahead. >> I said V didn't play last year. And then not having Garrett >> Sean didn't play last year and then not having Garrett and and him kind of moving inside, what skill sets have you seen from him to be successful there? >> Oh, yeah, Asante can ball, you know, he's played He's one of those guys in our room that's played a lot of football, you know, he's in our room now instead of the corner room. So, he definitely gets to, you know, see see his aspect of the game, you know, he's a baller, you know, he has good in coverage, good slot man. He's one of those guys that you can just go into and learn from as well. >> Kind of an offbeat question is like you had a 5-year college career, right? Because of the pandemic? >> I sure did. >> Wreck 'em. >> I'm wondering your perspective of seeing some of the rule changes in the NCAA. They're proposing the 5 years to play four. >> Nah, I ain't seen anything like that. I'm here where my feet are. >> Do you think with with 5 years a lot in college or do you think that >> Nah. you know my my second year was a covid year. I kind of didn't you know play a lot that year. So I kind of you mean I did five years but to me I just played four years, you know, I really didn't start playing until my third year, you know, I played running back in high school and then I got converted over to safety, you know, my first year I played second year got moved to corner and then all that went down after spring ball and then I got moved back to safety, you know, I really we had 10 games so you know, it was you know, here to miss or there didn't play a lot. My third year is when is when I really got comfortable you know, playing defense, you know, I never played it a down a defense even joking around in the backyard. I was always all time quarterback. I was a running back a receiver, you know, but got comfortable my third year and I feel like that's where my that's where my career started. So you know, just a crazy off beat story. This is my third year and I'm getting the opportunity to go, you know, earn a spot. So I kind of see it as that same that same build up is that I when I was in college going to my third year. So my third year means a lot to me as well as it did in college. >> Mike was saying there's a potential of three safeties on the field maybe at some point. How much does that allow you to really kind of be leaders on the defense? >> I mean we did the same thing last year. We played with three safeties, you know, I came in and did what I had to do. So there's nothing different at it nothing different about it at all.

title: Ben Johnson continues roster evaluation during OTAs | Press Conference
text: with the left tackle situation as Braxton kind of eases his way back into things. What do you hope you can see out of him this year that you can see a year ago? >> Well, we hope to see a healthier person. you know, last year at this time he was still still getting back into the groove and and certainly through training camp, it was a gradual process and um you know, as we we all know in this room that that that battle went on for a long time and uh took a while before we felt comfortable settling on Azie halfway through the season, but um you know, different circumstances this year. I think he's come back and uh his comfort level has risen just in terms of knowing what to do and how we want to get it done. and I think this is the best his body has felt in in a while as well. So, uh we're really encouraged with where he's at right now. >> What was your reaction to the Browns Rams trade yesterday? It's pretty big name trading places and coming to your conference. >> Um yeah, I not a whole lot of thought goes into it. I mean, that's uh got our own business we're taking care of right now. So, good. I know you were asking about Jayen Johnson last week, but what what have you seen from him since last week and what's he able to do and is he 100%. >> Yeah. Yeah, he's out there uh getting reps with the team and uh really pleased that he he's with his teammates right now getting to know them and and competing and working hard. So, um that's about the extent of it here here at this point of the springtime. >> And now that now that you're two weeks into OTAAS and you had this with with the defensive line and trying to strip things down the fundamentals, what's it look like now? Obviously, I know you'll know more when the pads are on, but just seeing DA and the coaches work a little bit differently with them like >> Yeah, I mean, we'll know everything when the pads come on. Like right now to evaluate offensive line and defensive line plays a little bit. Um, you know, fool's gold. Um, you always fall in love with some guys in the springtime and then that always changes. But I I'm really pleased with the teaching progression. I've been able to sit in some meetings and I love how the coaches are going about their business. I like how the players are responding to it right now. We're all on the same page. We're speaking the same language and uh that's always a good starting point. Oh my >> good. >> Now that you've got a year under your belt, how does it feel? How do you feel about your position, what you're doing, the people you're working? >> Somebody wanted to take their phone so I'm not interrupted again. >> Thanks. >> How does it feel to be a year under your belt going into your second year with what you've learned? >> Um, no. Oh, I I feel I feel really good about where we're at right now. Uh, you know, it was a certainly a maturation process for myself as well. We took a lot of time um this springtime looking at how last year went from a schedule standpoint to situations that arose in games to um you know, just a holistic view of how we can get a little bit better. And uh we're introducing some of that to our players right now. you know, we spent um the morning meeting going over a couple situations from last year that that hopefully we'll learn from and we'll be better from year two. So, uh you know, we're we're all striving to get better. It's no different for me as as the head guy. >> What has been your messaging to Rome? Uh now that DJ's gone and like that opportunity he has, >> same message as it's always been. We're trying to get a little bit better every day and uh trying to get a rapport with our quarterback, trying to get our system down pat and uh he's out there competing and and he looks pretty good right now. He was in a pretty frustrating he was in a pretty frustrating situation last year with the injury. How did you see him fight through that and and is that can that be helpful going into >> Yeah. Well, he's he's tough and I think that's what we all knew when he was coming out of college and certainly that makes you worthy of of uh where he was drafted. He's a team player. He he's going to lay it out on the line every time he gets on the on the grass. And so I think his teammates appreciate that. His coaching staff certainly appreciates that. and um you know hopefully we can get him 17 plus games this year and and uh you know he his career will really take off for that. >> What have you seen from Xavian Thomas so far on the field? >> Yeah, a player that's learning a rookie um but a guy that's working hard. >> With Kyler Gordon, I know that you've talked about just trying to get a formal relationship there and it made it difficult him being absent so much not playing last year because of injury. How important is it to get him on the field here in this I guess like this portion but also to training camp and having that consistency so you know the type of player you're going to have. >> Yeah. Well, I mean we we spoke last year and uh neither one of us were really happy with how how it went just from a a perspective of being available to get to know each other. Um I think he only played in three games when I when I look back at it. And so um you know this this spring was going to be a springboard for us to get going the right direction. And so, um, you know, we're still working through that. We're still trying to get that availability piece going. We know he's a good player when he's out there, but trust level is a huge thing for for this team, for this coaching staff, for the locker room. And, um, you can only develop that trust by being available. >> With with Jonah, I think Coach Roshar said that he was kind of the glue guy, a little bit of an unsung guy for your group last year. When you look back at his season here, what did you see in terms of what he brought to that offensive line? Yeah, it's everything that I I know about him. I've been with him since he was a rookie and uh I think he's a tremendous competitor. Um brings a a physical demeanor up front. Um and then when you pair him with a guy next to him like Darnell, you know, you can you can certainly displace the line of scrimmage and and dent that side of the line. So, um I think that came to fruition. Was really proud of him. He's he's always had to battle through some things himself and he was able to stay healthy throughout the year and and I agree with Dan. I think there's something to be said. He's he's somewhat of the spokesman up front there. Um he's played a lot of ball. He's played in big games. He's played at a high level. Uh as far as I'm concerned, he played at a Pro Bowl last year as well. Um certainly didn't get those accolades, but hopefully another another year fully healthy, he'll he'll get that recognition. >> Caleb was chosen to be on the the cover of Madden. Two questions. First, did you see the cover? Did you have any any thoughts? >> I saw it this morning. Yeah. >> No reaction. Just >> no reaction. Yeah. with all the spotlight and all the acclaim that comes his way, how do you do your part to make sure you keep him in the right head space with everything that that kind of follows him around? >> Well, I think he's he's wired the right way. He wants to be great and uh when it's when that's the case, you can coach him hard. Um, you know, we're showing clips in front of the offensive unit today and and there's some things from yesterday's practice that, in my opinion, he can get better at. And so, you coach him just like you coach all the rest of the guys. Um, and and he wants that. He wants to be coached the same. So, um, we meet every single day. Uh, that process has gone really, really well. We're seeing the game through the same lens, which I think is critical for a play caller and a quarterback to be able to do. And, uh, I'm really, really proud about how he's gone about this offseason so far. >> What do you like about joint about joint practices and and are you going to have more than one this off? >> Potentially. Yeah, we're still working through training camp scheduling right now. Um, but I know Zach came out and said that that we'll uh we'll go against Cincinnati. We're we're committed to that. We'll uh you know, I'm going to talk to him here in the near future. Hopefully, we can nail down some details, but uh there there's potentially more than just one this year. >> As a followup from Dan's question about Caleb Williams, a lot of people are projecting him all of a sudden based on what he did last year as a top five elite quarterback. Do you think he can get there this year or do you think he's already there? Yeah, I mean I think uh really what what we're all concerned about is is winning ball games. And so if that means top five quarterback based on wins, then I'm all for it. But that that's what we're concerned about is every single week going into the game, finding a way to win that ball game. I think he proved last year that uh if the game's closed at the end, he's going to go all out and and become Superman at times to to make some critical plays. So um that's great. We're continuing to see his evolution as a quarterback. Um, the accuracy continues to improve, the ball placement, the understanding of the offense, the orchestration of everything from the huddle to the the snaps, the shifts, the the cadence and all that. It continues to improve. So, that's all we really want to see right now. We're not going to judge. I don't know how you can judge top 10, top five. I think it's so subjective. So, um, he's on the right track and that's what we're concerned about. >> So, Chris and Courtney Ben, as you look for improvements from within, specifically with the defensive line, how does that apply to to Tez? what's kind of the next evolution for his game or the way that he can take it up a couple notches? >> Yeah, well, he he's mixed in with the rest of those guys just in terms of um as a whole, we didn't feel like our get off was very good. Um and so we're looking to improve that across the board. We feel like if we can if we can improve our get off up front um that that's going to help apply more pressure to the quarterback. Uh, so he's he's part of that equation as well, but he's still um one of those things that year two of this defense, I think things will slow down from our for our guys from a thinking aspect and so we'll be able to play faster. That's what I'm hopeful for for him along with the rest of those guys up front. >> On that note about sweat, um I know that Dennis and Jeremy have both talked about the coaching aspect of coaching those fundamentals with the pass rushers to get them, you know, to fix the pass rush. Where does that start? like what are you exact what exactly are you looking for? >> Oh, we're not giving out the secret sauce here today. >> What would what would success look like from from that aspect? Marrying the coaching with the players that you have like at this portion of the offseason. >> Yeah, I mean it's hard to judge this time of year once again with the upfront. We're not truly going after we're not bull rushing certainly. So, it it's a hard thing to gauge. We'll know more when we get the pads on in in training camp, but really pleased with how those guys are going about their business right now. everything we're we're coaching them to do makes sense to them. They're looking to apply it in a in a drill setting, in individual drills. Um, and so we'll see when when we get out there and we're playing real football, how much of an improvement we can make. End of the day, we're looking to affect the quarterback. It's a marriage of rush and coverage both, and we need to get better on both ends. >> Awesome. Back to you guys so quick.

We >> talked to Alex out there and Alex, right? He's a guy that was out there on the field talking to you a lot. Have you felt kind of that that welcome presence early on uh to the Cleveland Browns organization? >> Oh, yeah. 100%. Everybody I see, you know, quickly introduces themselves. I want to, you know, have a defined situation, just be able to do my thing every time without having to think too much, without having to slow down and read keys. And it is exactly that. I like it a lot. You >> you use the word upset. How how much does it motivate you now to kind of like prove them wrong that that they traded you? >> Yeah, I mean it's uh it's a different type of feeling, you know? I mean, I've always been doubted my whole life. You know, out of high school, I had the one offer, you know, going into college and, you know, leaving college, I was less doubted, but, you know, still had the little chip on my shoulder and everything like that. It definitely puts the chip on my shoulder. You know, when I was with the Rams, I was still learning how to play Dian, still learning how to be a football player, NFL player, and how to play at this next level. And the Browns, you know, got me. Now, I feel like they're going to get the best of me. They're not gonna get a half finished project or something you gotta work on. This is this is work here. This is gonna be the best version of me. That's everything I've done this off seasonason. It's gonna be great. >> How do you feel about the fact that uh you were the key to this whole trade and the Browns were not going to make this trade and part with Miles Garrett? Unless they could get you here. I mean, what does that, you know, say about how they feel about you? >> Yeah, I feel like that's a testament to not only me, but you know, my family, you know, how hard we work and everything like that. I feel like hard work never fails you. And to know that, you know, that this wasn't going to go through if I didn't wasn't a part of it. It's good to know that like that that was probably the biggest fact that you know brought some sunshine into this whole situation for me. I saw that I was like yeah they want me and it was cool. It was cool to know that. >> Your mindset stepping in at the same position for a guy who's done what Miles has done. >> Yeah. No, Miles is a great player. I watch his film every day. I, you know, keyed in on a couple things he does, the moves he makes, the technicalities of every small aspect of his game. I I very much studied him and to know that, you know, I'm not here to fill his shoes. That's not my job. That's not in my description in any organization I go to. That's not my job. My job is to be the best of me. If I'm the best of me, I'm not going to be, you know, Miles G. I'm not going to be Max Cosby, this guy, that guy, the best players in the league. I'm going to be the best Jared and that's going to be the best player in the league. >> There's no perfect time to be be traded, but to be traded where there's still some time in the offseason to go through mini camp, go through, you know, the OTA program, kind of learn and absorb a little bit before you jump into training camp. How beneficial is that going to be for you for the transition? Oh yeah, it's going to be amazing. You know, not only just the aspect of getting to know my teammates and the camaraderie, but to understand the playbook, understand what my job is specifically, understand every key aspect of it. Get to know obviously get to know my teammates. You know, when you have that camaraderie and everything like that, that elevates you from being a good team to a great team and we're going to be a great team. >> Dayton, Ohio. How does it feel just being back in your home state? Will you have family be able to travel up to Cleveland for some more more of your games? >> Yeah. Yeah, they'll definitely be able to make it. My most of my family's in Phoenix now, so my older sister is still in Dayton, though, so she's not too far away. But it's it's good to be back. I ain't going to lie. Hey, the clear blue skies. I landed on a great day. I I ain't got nothing much to complain about. >> What did your mindset turn from surprise and disappoint? Okay, new chapter. Let's go. >> Yeah, honestly, it was about took me about a couple hours. You know, I got home uh Braden Fisk, Byron Young both came to my house. They uh sat down with me, each of them, you know, individually. I got to sit down with them and talk to them and say my goodbyes and everything like that. And it was about when they left my when Fis left my house, I was like, damn. Like, all right, it's time to work. Like, you know, I don't get to be teammates with, you know, essentially my best friend no more. So, that was just the uh a bad factor of the party thing. I know you're still getting to know everyone, but the fact that you have Carson Sper on this defense and you two are the last two NFL defensive rookie of the year. Like, how how exciting is that potential pairing for? >> Man, that boy can fly now. He He can work. I like that a lot. I like knowing that that behind me that I can, hey, I don't got much to worry about if something, you know, I can play freely because I don't have to worry if something gets by me. He's going to be able to handle that. He's going to be able to clean everything up. So, now that's that's the exciting factor of this. >> You mentioned like your sort of journey to the NFL, you know, going off in high school and how you know it's kind of served motivation for you. Just how much has your path as unique as it was going to Albany and transfer to Florida State, how has that kind of molded you the person you are and the mentality that you I'm I'm used to uh you know hard situations. I'm used to having to deal with something hard and you know transfer that to being a better version of myself. I'm used to being at organizations or teams you know in college Aub you know the most winning team and everything like that. when I got to the Rams, you know, they was wasn't the most, you know, they they still was getting dubs, but they wasn't like, you know, up there like that. But, you know, every step of the way is just getting better. You know, I'm I'm excited to just keep working and and today was a big factor that watching the how the guys are in the weight room, how they are in the field, like them boys are flying. Like, I'm like, "All right, like y'all not messing around. Y'all y'all not going to lose again." So, we we not going to lose with the way them boys moving. Part of being upset about this in the initial going uh was the fact that maybe the Browns out there nationally uh don't have the greatest reputation in the world uh and that once you did get here and just get a feel for it a little bit, you're like this isn't anything like what you hear when you're when you're out there. >> Yeah. I mean, you can tell uh how a team is by how they practice. You you see losing teams practice terribly. You see great teams practice amazingly. It it translates. That's not a losing team out there. The way everybody was moving, I didn't get to, you know, get into the team situations today. You know, that's going to be another day. But the way the boys are moving, this isn't a losing team. Nobody's moving around like they're slow, like they're feeling sorry for themselves. People are moving like with intent, like they are not going to miss the opportunity to play in January, to play in February, to play in that big game. >> Is there any connection on this team to you? Any familiar face of your past? >> Uh, yeah, Jeremiah Bay is a I think he's a guard now. Me and him were at Floyd State together and KT Levenson. Me and him were at the Rams together. So two tackles I was messing up. >> There's only one mile scare obviously and you've already you know started your career really really well. just how do you I guess deal with coming in here maybe not replacing him but like you know you're you're the guy that they you know they traded him for and just you know what's what's your mentality coming in here maybe trying to fill those shoes as best as you can. >> Yeah. I mean you know I'm not I'm not here to fill anyone's shoes. Miles you know he's a size 13 you know Nikes whatever they are you know I'm a size you know 13 half size 14 Jordan's like everybody's different. I'm not here to fill his shoes. I'm here to bring my own. I buy my own. I'm here to work and I'm here to be the best version of me. The best version of me is going to be the best defensive player in the league. And the best defensive player in the league is going to play for the best defense in the league. And that's why I test like make myself testament too. >> How would you describe your game? >> It's violent. It's very violent. It's very mean. It's very um why are you in my way? I play angry cuz I'm like why do you think you can block me? And if you you know get the best of me, oh so you're game playing for me. All right. So I got something else for you. Like it's a very violent game when you're against me. J, I know you're just getting to know him, but what were your first impressions of both Todd Monkin and Mike Renber? >> Boys work. I I like it. Like I said, like them boys, everybody in here is working. Like it's not like a lack of like effort. That's the one that you can never say it's not a lack of skill. Them boys are working and they're doing moves. I'm like, "All right." Like the boys, everybody's good. I like it. >> You want to be yourself out here. So what is the first thing that the Browns fans need to know about you? What do you want them to know about the player, the person that's coming in to their city? >> Yeah, you know, I'm about a lot of things. I'm a big family person. I love my family. I love my friends. I care about, you know, the people that are close to me more than anything. But the one thing I hold above all, you know, besides God, because obviously God's above all, is work. Work is the most important thing to me. All I care about is lifting. All I care about is running. All I care about is how I can get faster, how I can get this step a little bit smaller, how I can, you know, translate this to the field. That's all I care about. And all I care about is being the best me. That's all that matters. >> Do you feel like perhaps there might be something to be said for kind of coming in here when the foundation of this team is being built? All you guys are so young. Uh this is the new core of a team that is probably going to be on the rise. Is there something to be said for that maybe over a really established team? Uh how do you feel about that situation? >> Yeah. No, I feel I feel great about it. You know, when you go into a younger team and a younger situation, a lot of people are their heads are all over the place. Some people are talking too much. Some people don't take this seriously. Don't take that seriously. That's not the problem here. Like the problem here is everybody wants to work too much. Like, hey, slow it down. Like, hey, let's figure out the little techniques of the stuff. Like, everybody here is like so focused, driven, and so wanting to be a best version of themselves. And I think that's like that's such a testament to just the new coaching staff and the new, you know, foundation that everyone's about to lay down. couple years when you were working with the Rams they had to rebuild that defensive line retiring and everything. How much that experience helped you to now carry on here? >> Oh yeah, I mean 100% that helped me uh you know exponentially like you go in with some of your best friends, some of the younger guys and you realize hey we might be a year apart, two years apart, but all we care about is how we can be the best version of us on that field. Sundays are the most important thing. So, we just spend so much time outside of football, outside of the team designated activities, watching film together, getting to know each other because when you know somebody, you play harder for him. >> Experience is huge in this I'm sorry. You said what? >> I said postseason experience is huge in this league. You've been in the league for a couple years and you have quite a bit already in such a short amount of time. This team obviously very young and inexperienced. What can you bring in terms of the playoff experience to the mindset of these younger players to to a team that that's their goal? Yeah, I mean, you know, during the regular season, every game matters. You know, the f first thing before even worrying about the playoffs is making the playoffs. You know, before even worrying about how we gonna win in the playoffs. And um once you get there, the margin for error is so small. You can't mess up. If you take one step too wide, boom, the B gap's wide open and they're running you for 60 yards down the field. You take one step too small, the edge is wide open and they're taking you 40 yards down the field, getting stopped at the one, and now they're in field goal range. The margin of error is so small in the playoffs, but before the playoffs, you even got to focus about the regular season. Before the regular season, you got to focus on the preseason. For preseason, you got camp. Before camp we got today. So, that's all I'm focused on right now. >> You have a you know, growing up in D. Did you have Were you a crowds fan or did you >> I ain't even honestly I ain't even watch football until I got to college. I was really was like just like enjoying life like I was being like a little kid out there messing around, playing in the sun and stuff like that. Just messing around. I I ain't watch football till I got to uh college and stuff. And I I still never had a favorite team. I just kind of lived.

title: Exclusive Interview with Andrew Berry
text: The man of the hour, executive vice president of football ops, general manager of Cleveland Browns, Andrew Barry, joining us live right off the top in studio. We like this weather. >> This weather will take you and me both. >> Yeah, there he is. There he is. >> There he is. >> Um, this was >> a surreal 24 hours, I think, for all of us. Um, and you I I thought you handled this about as well as you could yesterday at the at the foundation outing, which is a big day for us as an organization, obviously, but at the same time, you can't help what you can't help, and you can't control everything. Um and you know, in a situation like where you're dealing with a trade or a major transaction, um oftentimes you don't have sole control of the information flow. Um, and so it was one of those situations where, you know, we had a good outline in terms of how we were going to handle the communication, the messaging. Um, you know, let really the the afternoon be about all the good work that the Browns Foundation was doing. Um, you know, had worked with, you know, with uh LA and and they had done a nice job of of working with us in that. Um, and the closer you get to executing them, more people who maybe aren't even really a part of the the primary parties doing the deal, uh, become involved in it. And once it became apparent that, um, information was was was coming out and it was, you know, before, um, you know, LA had a chance to talk to to talk to Jared, um, we had to really adjust on the fly. So, um it was certainly different than we planned, but you know, at that point, you know, things were far enough along where we thought it was appropriate to um address our fans and address the local media in some form or fashion. >> Yeah. >> I'll say this. I thought you were very cool handling it when I walked in and I walked up to you and it was I knew that you knew and all of that and it was like and you were cool as a cucumber but it it was kind of a surreal thing being that we were at this foundation outing and I'll tell you there's a funny moment where where Todd came in and talked and then Todd's like I'll take a couple of questions and I was like oh boy and nobody asked thank goodness I didn't know how that was going to go but nobody asked but >> I mean we were sitting They were in the carts literally going to the first tea and then you heard everybody's phones around you'd be likez and then hey dude zig girl we traded miles and you know I'm sitt with JW Jinx is right there it was just like a to Glenn Glenn was I think right to my right >> everyone was there >> it was just a totally kind of a surreal moment and it's one that I think everybody who was there will certainly never forget >> a very memorable first Browns Foundation adding at Firestone huh >> no doubt no doubt for a great many reasons. All right. So, you talked a little bit about the the timeline earlier today of how this went together, but it it feels like from some things that have come out, like from a Ram standpoint that they've been determined to get this done for a long time. Jay Glazer said yesterday, we talked about it on the show that, you know, one of the reasons they drafted Tai Simpson and the word he used was because they quote knew they would not have a first round pick next year. So, it feels like this is a team that was very determined to get this done and and you guys were able determined to say, "Okay, if you want it, >> we need Jared Verse." Yeah, they they were they were very um persistent. They were very aggressive, which is their MO. Um and so, um it's it's certainly a credit to them because they they really forced the issue and forced us to um you know, kind of re-examine, you know, our approach, um you know, after the draft. And uh you know, like I said earlier today, it wasn't something that was plan A or or certainly expected. Um, but it got to a point where for us, you know, we thought it would it it would be irresponsible not to do the deal, quite frankly. At what point I had two-parter, which is horrible journalism, but at what point did you know that this was going to happen? And then how important was it to you because in in Glazer's reporting again, and we know he's pretty close with McVey, they didn't want to give up a player. They wanted to give up only picks. How important was it to you that not only was it a player, it was also that it was Jared Verse? Because >> in a situation where it's all picks, people could look at that and say, "We're already on to next year." When you trade a player of Miles Calibbo, but when you get Jared Verse back, it allows you to not only have assets for the future, but also say >> we're still really good on defense and have an elite edge rusher in a position where obviously nobody's Miles Garrett, but where we had an elite edge rusher before. >> Yeah, it's it's the right question, Nate. I'd say it's it's less actually about, you know, the perception of picks or picks plus players um and more about um I guess the merits of the deal. I think you're right that, you know, we we weren't super interested in a picks only deal for a couple reasons. I think number one, this is not your normal star player that's getting traded. And so the standard calculus of okay, you know, what's a first round pick worth? What's a what are two ones worth? um when you factor in the hit rate and when we talk about hit rate with picks, it's usually with starters are better. Um Miles is obviously on a different plane in terms of his his performance. >> Um and so it it doesn't quite match up like it would your standard trade. The second part of this is the timing which you alluded to where it's after the draft. It's really where most of the roster planning has occurred. Um what makes this trade different is if you look at you know S Garner for instance that trade or you look at um you know the the the Max Crosby trade that didn't necessarily go through Micah Parson's maybe a little bit different um but you usually are truly trading uh all present for future um >> because you're not getting something that um you know fills an onfield role uh at the area that you've that you've vacated. So for us, those two things taken in together make this different, especially when you factor in um how excellent of a player that Jared Verse is. Uh and that's what made it really really important to us because including Jared automatically raises the floor of the deal. It creates a very high baseline. um it's proven >> and you know the the you know the picks they they give you fantastic optionality, fantastic upside and real and potential. Um you know but with Jared it creates a very steady floor because there's realized potential already with um you know still more gains to potentially be realized. mentioned this morning that obviously when you go back two years and miles at the Super Bowl and the trade and all of that, then we get the new contract done and at that point I'm sure almost every team in the league calls you about him because he's Miles Garrett. Really? >> No. Yeah. I think there's I think there's um uh perhaps a little bit of a misconception with what happens when these when these um either mears become available or you know there's a trade request. So number one, every team in the NFL deals with trade requests, whether whether they become public or or not public. And so you kind of know it's part for the course. You can generally guess like which guys actually the team will be interested in moving versus the ones they won't. >> The second piece of it is I I guess the way I would equate it to is I think everybody in this booth and everybody on the call would love to have a $10 million home, right? Like we'd all love to have a but >> sounds great. there's a very small uh population of individuals that can actually afford it and it may be because of you know what they have in the bank account maybe because of you know what their cash flow issues. Um it's kind of the same thing in the NFL where it's like yeah like hey a player of great magnitude becomes available but does it actually fit for a team because of what they have to give up or you know even just taking on a contract taking on a contract of significance. So, um, it's it's interesting because the players at the extremes, there's usually probably a much smaller pool of teams that show or at least have legitimate interest um, than people would would maybe expect. So, where I was going with that and you you got there partly, the other part of it is he had a no trade. >> So, it's not only everything you said, but you mentioned the $10 million analogy. Most people who want to build a want who can afford a $10 million house want to build exactly what they want. And so there was that component with Miles as well. So while people would say that maybe the whole league would call, okay, fine, but then there's only so many who can afford it, there's only so many that can make it work, and then there's only so many that Miles would say yes to because he has the no trade. Yeah, I'd say that probably had maybe a little bit less of an impact just to be truthful because it's not a situation where okay, you're setting out uh if if like if it was a plan A, you would then, you know, partner with with Miles in this situation like okay, like what's the destination of teams, things like that. There was really nothing like that in play because it wasn't a primary, you know, consideration. So it's not like hey if a player has a no trade clause on the front end they submit hey here's a list of teams that that you know I'll approve approve you know approve a trade to. So like that is true that uh >> look there's there's probably a subset of the teams in the NFL that um you know he would have been comfortable going to but that was never part of this particular calculus because there was never really a there was never really a discussion on that. And to your point, there are only so many teams, if you guys were resolute in your belief that there had to be a young edge coming back that had was a proven, as you said, proven potential with more room to go. There are only so many teams that have that >> that would even consider trading that player that also would consider trading that player to get this much better today to try to win. I mean, the Rams in some ways it's absolutely perfect. Storms demo there. there. I don't think they've made a first round pick other than before this year and I think it was verse was the only one and now he's not on there. Doesn't even see any couldn't have been any better. Defensive rookie of the year and a two-time Pro Bowler. >> Yeah, I think that's right. I mean it's it's it's a it's a very particular fit um for all the parties involved and um you know it's I think it's unusual for something like this to come to together the way that it did. What was the thinking in it's a 271 which we know those are hard assets to get and we talked about this yesterday there you were able to get two of the three 27 picks that were traded in the draft. Now you have another 271 and that's clear to me that's one of those where it's like the league is in unison or at least they seem to be on the same page that this is a draft that people find valuable. It just seems the way people are operating with 20ome picks. How did it end up with a 28-2 a 293? What was the thought there and how did we arrive there? Yeah, I think, you know, for any team it's hard to like wipe out a single draft essentially. Like I don't I don't think you'll Ricky Williams. >> Yeah, I don't think you'll ever see like the Ricky Williams, you know, type type trades to be honest. Um, so it's just it's a lot easier to spread it out over multiple years. I also think for us, um, you know, it's helpful to be invested, I guess you could say, across seasons. Um, because the reality is you can always move assets forward, you know, whether it's for, uh, whether it's for a player, whether it's for another pick. Um, but if you're like overindexed in a singular year, you know, there there does become a little bit of an extra expiration date where you you can be oversaturated. I mean, we like where we're sitting heading into next year's draft with 11 picks and um, you know, obviously the two first rounders, the three fourths and the two fifths. Um, and that's before we make any trades. Uh but there does become a certain point where it's it becomes a little bit uh more inefficient in terms of how you deploy those >> diminishing marginal utility. >> That's exactly right. >> Last one I have for you on the mile side. Um you know whether it's S Parsons, Quinnon Williams, Max Crosby. Jared Verse was a first round pick. He's proven in the league. I mean, I'm sure it's mixed when you deal with Miles because I mean, you've known him so well and all of that, but at the same time, like this has been a massive undertaking. Two drafts, one yet last year that looks like you just knocked it out of the park. Feels like this year's looks pretty dang good right away, too. What What What has this been like for you this this off season? That side of it? >> You know, honestly, it it I don't mean to sound callous. It's really been business as usual. So, that's and that's different for me emotionally, just quite honest, just because I've known him for a decade. You know, known him since he's 21 years old. Um but the general, let's say the the roster churn and bringing in new faces and um you know getting younger at certain spots, turning over different rooms. The Miles trade and and there are cap implications for that and and money that is available maybe now to the Cleveland Browns as you swap some of those things out and then the postjune 1st cuts of David Njoku and Joel Batonio that money comes back now, right? >> Uh effectively, >> this probably not the best characterization of it honestly. uh you know, Nathan, like uh a lot of our planning this offseason, how we structure our deals, it's so that we can function in March regardless of you know, when um the postjune 1 roster transactions occur. Um so all of that's already really been factored in. Sundays are the most important thing. text: Well, Miles, I know you've heard it a thousand times today, but I'll say it again. Welcome to Los Angeles on your first day as a Ram. It's great to sit down with you. title: Why Texans believe they're legit Super Bowl contenders, how they stack up across NFL
text: Hi guys, Aaron Wilson talking tonight about the Texans Super Bowl chances and something that Will Anderson Jr. said the other day really resonated with me. He had a little time with the team after the practice. They're breaking it down and this is a time when Wills, you know, showing his leadership as a team captain and discussing just the chances for the team. And he said, "If you believe," this is his message to his teammates, "If you believe that we're a Super Bowl team, raise your hand." How many of you guys out there are raising your hand? And he challenged everybody because he said, "Everybody that's here, they brought you here because they think you're a Super Bowl caliber player." So he looks across the team, he thinks they're certainly Super Bowl caliber, and he's thought that for the whole time they've been there. He says, "Everybody's locked in. He feels very good about everybody, has the buy in. He says it's the best OTAAS they've ever had." Well, that's all fine and well, and I do think the Texans are certainly a playoff contender, but are they ready to take the next step? And there's some reasons why I think they will, and a few reasons why I think they might not. And a lot of that has to do too with the balance of power within the entire NFL. So, we'll go through that a little bit and we'll hear from Will, of course, at length on this topic. We'll talk a little bit about the roster and where I think it's well stocked and where I think it could still stand for some improvement. So, you know, just looking at the Super Bowl odds. Well, they just tilted a little bit. They changed. title: General Manager Nolan Teasley’s Full Introductory Press Conference | Minnesota Vikings
text: Good morning everyone. Great to be with you all and thank you all for being here. When we set out to find the next general manager of the Minnesota Vikings, we were looking for someone with a strong football acumen and a clear vision of team building. Someone who appreciates and understands our culture and history, is an effective communicator and consensus builder, and is respected across the NFL. There is no question Nolan Teasley fits each of these criteria and we are thrilled to add someone of his caliber to our organization. Nolan brings a tremendous football background in the role and a proven track record of success over the past 13 seasons with the Seahawks under the tulage of John Schneider. Nolan was a part of nine playoff teams, three Super Bowl appearances, and two championships. He has a strong understanding of talent evaluation at both the collegiate and professional levels, is adept at building a consistently competitive roster, and brings a disciplined, process-driven approach to this job. He understands schematics and player traits at a high level, and that knowledge quickly earns him credibility with each coaching staff. What really impressed us in our discussions with Nolan and with people around the league was his wide range of experiences. We have a high level of respect for John Schneider and John put Nolan in a position to increase responsibilities in every aspect of football operations and allowed him to be a key voice in all areas of roster building. That experience paired with Nolan's confident but humble presence stood out throughout this search. Ultimately, this was an extensive process that brought us multiple candidates we believe will be future general managers in the NFL as well as a strong internal candidate in Rob Brzinski. Rob is the consumate professional. For more than 25 years, he has demonstrated his character and leadership, and no one cares about the Minnesota Vikings more than Rob. His institutional knowledge and experience remain invaluable and he will be critical to our future success. Putting Nolan together with Rob and Kevin gives us three strong leaders with complimentary skill sets and we're confident that this is the best outcome for the Minnesota Vikings. I want to thank Turnkey ZRG along with Andrew Miller and Kevin Okonnell for assisting our ownership group through this process. There is no question we improved as an organization. Nolan and Morgan, we are so proud to welcome you and your children to the Vikings family and to the state of Minnesota. We're confident you will love becoming part of this community. With that, it is my pleasure to introduce the next general manager of the Minnesota Vikings, Nolan Teasley. good morning. Um just going to take a minute. This is uh this is amazing. Um going to start by thanking you know the staff for being here, members of the media. Um, I just want you to know that I'm I'm excited to to be working with you moving forward into the future and I look forward to meeting uh and getting to know each each one of you on a personal level. Thank you to Mark Wolf, to Ziggy Wolf, to the to the Wolf family for providing me this opportunity. Thank you to Kevin Oonnell. Thank you to Andrew Miller uh for providing me this opportunity. I cannot wait to get to work and I'm looking forward to to moving forward into the future with you guys. They are not here today, otherwise our youngest, Nash, would have already made his presence known, but I want them to know how much I love them. Uh, the the roster, it's obvious it's a strong nucleus of talent on both sides of the ball. They've won a lot of football games here in the last four years, including five in a row to end last season. title: Alvin Kamara showed he wants to be in New Orleans
text: Alvin Kamara is back, reported the OTAs today, and took part in practice, went through everything, went in the locker room, did a media session, business as usual for Kamara as his situation with the Saints continues to define itself. This video is presented by Matt Bowers Auto Group. I got to admit, it Alvin showing up might be like the funniest thing that could have happened today. I was not expecting it. I don't think anybody was expecting it. He usually works out off on his own in Miami with his trainers. He goes through all his stuff. He gets ready for the season. He has his process and he's had his process forever, but today he decided to show up. He said he was laying in bed last night, decided to jump on a plane, flew over here, got here about 1:00, came, went through a practice, and it was business as usual, man. It was It was good to see him out there. He didn't do a whole lot in the practice, went through individual drills, but he spent some time talking to Travis Etienne, and those two spent a good amount of time together on the sidelines just kind of chopping it up and getting to know each other. And then he, you know, observed a lot of what was going on in the practice. So, when he goes out there and practices in full, like there'll be a little bit of a ramping up period, and I don't expect really to see Alvin back out there until mandatory mini camp, but look, this isn't about the practice. It isn't about the OTAs. It isn't about anything. It's Alvin showing up. My interpretation of it is just saying, "Hey, look, I want to be here. I want to be part of this team. I want to practice. I want to be part of the Saints. I want to finish my career here. I want to figure this out." This was him showing that, and I think I think that's a big step. Look, if I had to guess if there was ever any tension between the Saints and and Alvin, I think that would exist in his contract. There's clauses in there about de-escalators on his salary for or not practicing in OTAs and all this stuff, and him showing up is is an olive branch. Hey, look, this is This is me showing up. This is me doing my job. This is me letting everybody know this is where I want to be. There's no beef on my side. He literally said there's no beef on his side with anybody and you know, I I wouldn't expect there to be. Um he was asked at one point if uh he would be willing to take a pay cut. He didn't answer that question, but I thought his answer was incredibly revealing. He said, "You know, if they ask me about it, it's something, you know, we'll we'll find out then." title: Saints DB Justin Reid on managing expectations, Jonas Sanker taking reps at slot, Julian Blackmon
text: So, guys are making plays. Guys are excited. The defense feels a lot tighter as far as like, you know, open windows making it hard on on our offense. And it's been fun. Having a blast with it. >> How different do you think this team is going to be without, you know, Alshon Jeffery, DeMario, you know, a couple couple of new new faces? >> Yeah, absolutely. I think it's going to be a combination of everybody else stepping up to the plate, bringing their own influence and juice, and you know, everyone has some accountability in what we're putting together and we're going [laughter] to put a good product on the field for for our fans and for the city. So, um we're excited about that. We're close. I mean, our room feels like it did in college. My guys hang out, we know each other, we have some history with each other. Um our level of communication is premium. You know what I mean? We're not We're not trying to win the off season competition of, you know, going to announce and whatever, right? You going to let your play do the speaking for yourself. Don't overlook anybody. This is the NFL. Every opponent is a good opponent. So, even if there's a game where you're picked to win by 20 points, you still got to go out there and earn it. You know, and then it's just day-by-day, and then you need to play your best ball when you get into November, December. Right? You want to start out hot and fast and everything else like that. You want to maintain your health, but you really want to get things right and play together, play your best ball heading into the postseason. And from there, just believe in yourself. [snorts] Nobody needs to go out and be superhuman. You just got to be the best version of yourself. And you know, if everyone's you got 11 guys doing that, you're going to come out with some good results. >> Justin, just getting Julian back. Yeah, obviously he only played in one game last year, but he was a big part of that room. Like what has that been like? >> Oh, huge. I mean, Julian, he's a versatile guy, so he has a ton of experience. Me and him get along really well. One of my best friends on the team, so it's fun being out there. Talking with him in the game, our communication level because I'm so comfortable with each other is really high. And just being able to disguise and sometimes switch responsibilities, like hey, let's give him a different look. I will go here, you go here. Or next time let's flip it and see if that, you know, changes things up. He makes a ton of plays, ball hawk, willing tackler, fun guy to play with. >> And just Jonas, year two, kind of changing positions a little bit. You know, what has been your thoughts on him so far? >> Oh, huge. I mean, Jonas one of the smart guy, can play everywhere. Extremely fast. One of the things I told him ending last season was, hey, whatever whatever you do, don't lose that speed. As long as he can run, he can play, especially in this DB field, so he makes plays on the ball. Probably should have had a couple more picks than he had even last year, but he didn't have a chance to make those in this game. >> And what are the biggest differences going from the safety spot to the to the nickel spot? >> Safety you can see a lot more, right? So safety you can kind of see motions, you can anticipate, you can kind of make calls. Nickel is a lot more feel. Like when you're closer to the closer you are to the line of scrimmage, the less you see. Right? So, you just have to feel what's happening, feel the combinations. You got to trigger a little bit faster. Um you got to set the force. And you also have to play knowing that there's a guy behind you who can make you right. You know, so the most important thing is to make a decision quickly and just go for it. When you're safety, you're kind of like the the fix-it man. Like you you have a gap, but if somebody ends up in your gap, then you got to go replace whoever they were supposed to be. You know, so the safety is a little bit more patient. Um Nick is a little bit more of a quick safety. >> Julian's return like kind of allows the defense to put notice there as well. Like >> Yeah, I mean we start we're like um we have a ton of guys that are versatile. So, Julian has experience playing nickel. I have experience playing nickel. Jonas is getting some very valuable reps right now learning to play nickel. So, that versatility in in three ways it allows us to maintain, you know, the system and what Coach Daily wants to do. >> That's what happens. That Coach Daily wants to put the best players on the field right now. And that means finding a way um to have Julian and Nick on the field. Nick is more than athletic enough, more than smart enough, more than willing enough to play nickel. And he's going to he's got to do it. >> Were you doing any package last year as you like had to play nickel again? Like how did you kind of assault the role? >> We had a package last year too where we had a a big nickel in some light third and fourth situations where we wanted to bring more, you know, sweep in the box. And whatever position you need, you know, any one of us to play, we're all willing to do it for the good of the team. >> Just because there are multiple guys who have the ability to do it, do you find more value in multiple guys kind of rotating in and out of that spot? Or is it more valuable to say this is your role, be really good at your role if that makes sense? >> You want to be good at something first. I do think you want to be good at really good at something first, which is why I think he's taking the majority of those reps right now. It's not as hard to switch between one and two. But as a young player, you do want to focus on one thing first. Sanka's had a ton of experience as a rookie year playing safety. So he can do both and he has the intelligence to handle both. >> Do you have a message for Sanka's fans? >> Yeah man, we we want we want we want that stadium rocking. We want y'all to come home, show out. We want like with me growing up watching Saints football, I wanted it to be like 2009 where you walk in there, you can't even hear yourself think. You hardly have a conversation with the person next to you. We want that type of energy and we want to be able to earn that. We want to be able to earn bringing you guys into the stadium to bring that energy.
