Man, I never knew. Maybe we can use Joel Batonio. Thank you, Howie Roseman. You've made us all better. Everybody, have a great day. We'll talk to you soon. Uh, be well. Till then, bye-bye.

title: Odell Beckham Jr.: 'I'm here to earn it' | New York Giants
text: How'd it feel out there for you? >> Feels great. Um, you know, I had a lot of time off to taking a step away from the game was what was best for me. Um, at a time in my life where, you know, you love something so much that it kind of became detrimental. It became bad to me. And just being able to take that time off and be with my son and be with family and just uh rep prioritize what was important to me. Um, and knowing that, you know, I still love this game so much. It felt great just being back out there, being back in the building, just on this field, looking at this stadium. Um, it's a pretty surreal feeling. So, I know I got a lot of work to do. I know Harbs and I have already talked about it. Like, I came here to I came here to earn anything, you know, everything in my life. Nothing was given to me. Um, so I came here to earn it. Just work hard every day and uh be the best I can for the team. for a non-cont practice. You took a couple of pops today. Uh first time you've you've kind of taken something like that in a while. How'd that feel? >> Well, they hit they hit harder than my son. My son's been beating me up. But it um you know, I think it's still, you know, people don't want to get beat by me, so they going to make sure they going to make sure that they do what they can. But, you know, it feels good. It's football. Um it's definitely been a minute, but it feels good. It's fun. Um I've been needing it. and I've been missing it. So, you know, I'm just happy to be here. >> Odell, you use the word surreal to be back here. When does it go from surreal to reality for you that you have this opportunity? >> Uh, pretty quick. I think it was surreal being here and then like you say, you take a couple hits and you're like, "All right, well, now I'm here." So, um, I definitely feel like I'm living in the present, not thinking about the past and not thinking about the future too much. Just, uh, enjoy the moment. you know, you're prepared for it and make the most of the opportunity. You know, like I said, I can't think of a single thing in my life that was given to me. Um, everything was earned and I really wouldn't want it any other way. >> Odell, do you know what you are as a player right now? >> Uh, a veteran, you know. Um, it it's definitely been some time, but you know, we they got a lot of measurements and numbers, and I look at all the numbers, and I'm still just as fast, as fast, faster. Um, it's just about being back in football. It's different than just training, you know. So, uh, like I say, it just felt good to be back out there, be around bodies, hit the ground, play football. It's like it's what I've done all my life. Um, and I just feel like I was watching the last bit of the Raphael the dog doc and it's just about he was talking about how, you know, he pushed it to the limit. And I think for me, my whole life, for better or for worse, is pushing it to the limit. And um just the way that I had to to walk away, um it was just unsettling in my soul, in my spirit. It's not who I am. I've never surrendered or quit or felt like I given up on myself or or anything. Um and it just wasn't sitting with me. So wasn't sitting with me well. So I had to I have to do this. This is for myself. this for my son. I want to lead by example. I want him to be able to see who I am, you know, not like who I was. Um, and just know that, you know, we never give up in our house, you know. Um, and you go after what you believe in. You believe in yourself. Um, and at the end of the day, God going to take care of the rest. >> From a spiritual standpoint, how are you contextualizing having to be in the circumstance of having to earn it? you know, when you think about all the way that you came into the league, the glitz and the glamour of everything, everything you've been through on and off the field, and I I know you look at things through a guideline, too. Why do you think at this point in your life now that you are in a circumstance of having to earn it, so to speak? >> Well, you know, when I came here as a rookie and I kept pulling my hamstring, I remember it might have been a few people in this circle who was not very sure about who I would be. Um, couple words thrown around here and there. If we forget about it. Um, but it was it it's just how I am. When I was at, you know, coming out of high school, I was the fourstar. I was the underdog. I went to LSU. I wasn't the top receiver. I ended up starting my freshman year. I get to the league. I wasn't the first receiver drafted. I'm, you know, I always had to earn it. I always had to prove it. It's just been who I am. And it was always about proving it to myself. there's, you know, there's always a little bit you want to prove it to everybody else, but like deep down inside to me, it was about proving it to me and believing in me. Um, and believing in what God had given me and my abilities and all that. So, um, I like it this way. I I feel like it's going to bring it's going to elevate me. It's going to bring me up to have to earn it. Um, you know, coach and I talked about that. I think that was one of his fears. He was like, I love you so much and I got so much respect for you. like I don't want to bring you here and then have to cut you or whatever. And I'm like, listen, >> I'm going out on my sword either way it goes. So, if that's what you got to do and you see that I'm not best or or fit, then you know, by all means, I'm good with it. I could live with it. I can't live with sitting sitting at home like not doing not doing it. You know, I just couldn't do it. Um, like I say, it's not who I am. So, I'm just here to enjoy the moment, work hard, and um you know, we'll see what happens. >> What is it about Harbaugh that >> What is it about Harbaugh that you respect? >> You know, when they were I kind of got a little call when they were looking at coaches and won't say any names, but I mentioned him specifically. Um I was in Baltimore. Um this is a man of God. This is a leader of men. Um and truly from a football aspect what in those meetings how attentive he was and and those little things that come up in the game that sometimes you often take for granted like he's very much on it you know um and and he leads in a very good way uh and and he just was one of my favorite coaches that I ever had. So I was spoke very highly of them when they asked me about who should be here. Um and I believe they got just the right man for the job. someone who could actually change the culture or uh at least start it in the in the right direction. >> Who asked you? >> You know, somebody healthwise. Harbaugh said one that from a knee standpoint he thinks you're healthier than you were in Baltimore and two that this Monday you looked even healthier than April. So, where is your health? How do you feel? And what have you been doing to keep up? >> Uh, I'm feeling good. I just been working at home. Just being honest with you. I've been at EXO's back in Arizona and we just been getting after it and yeah, Baltimore for me was it was tough because it was like right after the surgery and then kind of playing the whole year knowing you needed to do like a little something but you don't have the time. Uh it was just difficult, you know, and then I kind of wasn't playing as much. So then there was a lot of things that were going on. Um but I feel good. Um now I'm like I said I'm I'm fast. I'm moving well. It's just now about the repetition, you know, getting building up your football endurance, uh, back to the football IQ, knowing your spatial awareness, knowing where people are at, things that'll, you know, they'll they'll come back, but, you know, every, like with everything else, it takes a little practice. >> What's the best case scenario in this second game with the Giants? Like, what do you want to see happen here? >> Um, I think play play well, win the Super Bowl. That's the best case. You know, that's what you want to do. You know, I I used to be in here looking at these banners and all I ever wanted to do for this place was win. You know, everybody knows you could write up however you want, but like I never wanted to leave here. I just came from a school where if we lost on Saturday, like my season was over with. So, I hate losing. I hate it. I hate it. And all I ever wanted to do was win. And um that's all I want to do now. So, it's just like everybody else who's practicing right now. Like, everybody wants to win a Super Bowl. We're not coming in here to like good season and then get to offseason. like we all want to win that Super Bowl. So, that's a goal, but knowing it's a lot. It it takes a lot to to do that. Um, I've been there before. So, I'm just trying to be whatever I can for this team and and be the best version of myself. >> Odell, what's your connection with Jackson? I mean, I know you have some relationship of some sort with him. And what do you see from him as a quarterback, maybe your last quarterback here? >> He's he's very good. Um, you know, and I watched him last year and, you know, he likes to have fun. like he he enjoys the game of football and that's something great to see um from a young quarterback. He got an arm on him obviously he's got all the swag and the only connection we really have is LSU used to beat the hell out of miss so that's about it >> speaking how okay >> how much does it mean to you that John Mara and the Giants wanted you back and what how much does that relationship mean to you in the context of returning >> It means a lot. you know, we we had been in touch like over the years and seeing him and now seeing the kids and they're growing up, you know, I remember when they were all in in kids jerseys. Just being able to be here and and see Mr. Mirror, it's like, like I said, I want to win it, but it's like I want to do it bad for like this family. This family brought me in. They gave me my first opportunity. Um something I'll forever be grateful for. So many amazing memories. You know, my life was here. Um and I never thought I'd be anywhere else. So, just to even have the opportunity to put a jersey and a helmet back on, I actually left one of my helmets here. It had dust on it. Uh, so it was good to see. But, um, yeah, I want to I want to do it for for that family, for this building, for Giants, Giant Nation. You know, this is this was my this was my squad. So, um, like I say, it's just going to come with everyday work. Uh, and and just be the best be the best me I could be. >> Three more. Three more. Odell, what kind of >> How old are you? Why you ask me? >> Older than that. >> Okay. >> What kind of resource do you think you can be for Malik Neighbors who's been like you were great on the field going through an injury like you have and has had some moments in his career where he's, you know, question coaching or question play things that you went through early in your career? >> Yeah. Um, I think I could be a great uh asset for him. You know, even when I wasn't here, I was hitting them up. I'm like, "Yo, no offense, but it's like I know how they are. Like, I know how they going to turn it and living do it. Just telling you." Um, and he's also he comes from that school. He comes from like we come from the same place. Like, we want to win that bad. Now, there's a way, you know, to do everything. And I think just with everybody else, like everybody learns from their own ways and mistakes. Like my son is going to have all the game in the world, right? But he's still going to grow up and as an adult, he's going to make his own mistakes and I'mma be there to pick him up and, you know, maybe give some advice for the next time that he could carry. But at the end of the day, he, you know, he's a grown man. He's gonna make his decisions. And I think um I think when you go through an injury like that uh it really it really for a minute it hardens you but then it also it gives you a lot of experience. It gives you a lot of you know knowledge and you get to learn a lot about yourself. So I think through this process um which is has been a tough process but I think he's going to come out on the other end better and I can't wait to see him back on the field. Uh obviously we know what kind of player he is so just however I could help him anybody else. Um, trust me, I know all the things to do and I know the things not to do. So, >> I >> Yeah, >> you're 33. >> Okay. Which in I think it's young, but in football terms, it's not, you know, it's not that young. You've had some serious injuries to your legs. Yeah. >> How much do you view this as sort of like your last chance to, you know, keep this going? Again, like I was saying, I was watching the the Raphael doc and it was like just seeing all the things he's gone through and it's like just for me, some people just have that heart. Like I got up, tear my knee, I get up again, I get up, I'mma get up off that ground, you know, and um you said 33 like it's dog like but um no like you know I'm still moving at 20 21 miles an hour. I'm still you know finding ways to get open. And it's just like you're it's not going to be the 195 lb 2014 number one receiver who knows the ball's coming to him every single time. I can kind of, you know, cheat with a lot of things. Like it'll be very attentive to detail, very uh locked in and knowing like, okay, this is your opportunity, you know, just it's just a different game. Um, but I'm still ready, you know, 33. It's a great age. >> Last chance. Uh, I I look at it like this. Um, God's given me one more opportunity to play. And whatever I do with that is that, you know, I'm not saying that this is my only year. Um, and I'm not saying that I got five more for you. I'm just looking at it like this is my opportunity now. And, uh, we'll see where it goes from there. >> Odell, you mentioned you mentioned the past and, you know, now moving forward. Do you have any regrets that you carried with you for a while about here how things ended? What you may have done, taken upon yourself, and how have you been able to kind of >> equate that and, you know, come to some sort of peace with how things ended? >> Yeah, I think I I I took it with me in other places and being like, you know, I know what I don't want to do, but at the end of the day, like I said, I never wanted to leave here. I just wanted us to have a better team, you know, better people, better players. Um, sound like a Papa John's version or something, but I just wanted to to be great and and I care about it like that much. Um, as far as regrets, I'm kind of one of those people who for better, for worse. It's like never regret anything cuz at one point in time, it was exactly what you wanted. So, I don't hang my hat on it. I learned from it. Um, if I regret anything, it would be not winning here and not being the guy that I know that I could have been and allowing things to to get in the way of that. Um, so other than that, I wish that things could have went differently, but they went exactly how they were supposed to. I always trust and believe in God and his plan, and, you know, maybe if I would have stayed here, something worse could have happened. You know, I just I take it for what it is. Um, and like I say, want to make the most of the opportunity now.

title: DJ Reader on Joining the Giants' D-line | New York Giants
text: What was um the process like with coming here where obviously you had the visit then waiting till after the draft. Just take us through those couple of weeks and months. >> Uh I think you know you I came on the visit liked it obviously uh had some good conversations with the coaches, the staff and um then you leave and your agent and them try to figure it out. That was really the whole thing. I I had some family stuff to take care of. So just trying to figure out what what the process would be about like somebody want me. I knew um I was going to have to report a little bit later because of what I had going. So, >> did you always think it would be here? Cuz I know you go to Baltimore, too. I mean, I don't know. >> Uh yeah. No, not that I always thought it was going to be here. You know, early in the process, you don't you're just trying to go where who's interested. Then I got here and you kind of realize like we have some pieces here that are really really special that you don't have in a lot of places. And um I think it came down to that and then um the enthusiasm of just talking with the coaches, how they felt about it. Um Ben had a lot of respect for Harbs and seeing him work for some years and you know he he's seen it all and the excitement you kind of saw on his face about like the opportunity was kind of cool. So I knew it would be a good opportunity if I end up coming here. >> When they spoke to you initially, right, Dexter Lawrence was still here. >> Mhm. >> Right. And were those conversations about you and Dex together? >> Um and then obviously now you were technically with his replacement. >> Not necessarily his replace. Yeah, I guess um I think most of the conversation was just more about adding to the room um whatever was in the room. Um I knew it was a possibility they were going through what they were going through with Dex. Um and so that was what it was. It didn't really kind of it would be cool obviously to play with him. Got a chance to text him and talk to him, but it wasn't something that played too deep into my decision. And it was more so I wanted to be at a place with some good pieces and um it was kind of just explained like you know we hope we can get it done and if we can't then you know we'll we'll make sure it's compensated if we don't but you know we we want to get it done and you know things just didn't go that way. So was what it was. >> There are analytic sites that say Dexter Lawrence was the most double team player in the NFL >> and that you were the second most double team player in the NFL. How do you handle those double teams and what kind of resource do you think you could be to the edge rushers here if you're commanding those double teams? >> Uh I think it's something that kind of comes with the territory of the position. Um and you kind of just got to know it is what it is. It's smart our offensive scheme. I'm the guy kind of closest to the center and the guard. So I'd probably double team me too. Um safety down usually to a lot of the nos and sides and a lot of defenses. So it's kind of just how it goes. Um, but I think I've always done a good job of just kind of taking that in stride. Um, knowing that it's important for those guys who really put pass rush and they do this on a daily to be the guys who are going out there and getting, you know, getting pressure up the middle so quarterback can really roll to them. And um, I've always had good edges and I think my edges usually have good seasons when they've played with me. So, it's been good. >> You talked about the pieces in this room, this defense. What when you looked at it, what specifically attracted you when you see this defense that you wanted to join? >> Um, you got like a if you kind of look out there, I know y'all are at practice, they kind of got like a get off the bus type of team. You look out there's a bunch of big, strong, fast guys running around and like that's exciting. Um, when you're playing on defense and, you know, you see the special pieces on the edge. You got three edges that, you know, are proven can play. um guys in the middle, safeties, linebackers, it's it's a team you kind of want to be around. Then on offense, it kind of speaks for itself. I don't get too deep in the offensive side of the ball. That's that's their thing. But um on defense, it was just you look at the guys, you see what's in your room, you kind of A lot of teams aren't really built like that. And um if you can get it right and put it together, it can be special. >> Anything else? >> Boom. >> What's your relationship with Shelby? Do you have one? You guys signed at kind of the same time. Do you just from being in the league? >> Yeah, just from being in the league. A lot of respect for him. A lot of mutual friends. Uh nothing crazy. I'm excited to get a chance to really talk to him, be around him. Um but uh yeah, a lot of mutual friends. Heard really, really good things about him. And I've always respected his game and him as a man.

title: Julian Love On The Safety Group 'The Competition Level Is Really High' | Seattle Seahawks
text: How's your off season been doing? >> It's been good. Yeah, just kind of enjoying time with the family. What's the vibe like? >> The vibe we had kind of messing around with each other, you know, late in the season last year. It is the same now. He was just a great friend, great locker room presence for us. Uh but then like our room now is just a lot of different personalities still and the competition level is really high like you know group one through three or four or whatever. Um everyone is doing the extra work. Guys are meeting early. Scratch that. Guys are getting together and talking and texting with each other just trying to coordinate. Um you call that uh players are texting with each other just trying to figure it out. Uh scheme stuff and stuff like that. Um just because you know we're everyone's trying to be the best. Everyone's trying to you know show what they got and yeah the additions that we have in that room is I love it. >> Julian, what do you uh think Noah manag brings to >> I think he brings a sense of like competition. Uh Noah from the jump. He's he's out here he's in the weight room lifting with Derek Hall. Uh one of the strongest guys on the team trying to just like one up him. Maybe it's like an Auburn thing. I don't know. Uh so he brings the competition. He brings experience. He brings a maturity to him. Uh and he's a pro. Like he goes about his routine even though we're in OTAAS's. Um yeah, you can see, you know, why he's been rated as a high caliber player just he's a pro every >> day. You you've obviously have the flexibility to play different spots. I know like when Kobe was down, you kind of shifted what you're doing. >> Yeah. >> Do you go into a season where there's going to be with Kobe gone and kind of telling the coach like, "Hey, figure out how it works and where you need me or do you say like this is kind of where I want to be?" >> Yeah. I think it's the first thing. I think naturally I'm always like just throw me in at whatever and I'll play that role. Just like fit, you know, cater the defense to where everyone else feels comfortable. I probably should stop doing that. I probably should like, hey, this is kind of, you know, this is what I do. This is my role. This is what I'm best at. Let me go out and do that. Um, I think there's a sense of that um because we have so much versatility. I think Bud brings a lot to the table. Ty brings a lot to the table. Nick brings, you know, everything to the to the table on defense. Um, and so it allows me to kind of, you know, be myself, play my role, um, and do what I do best, uh, thankfully. >> What's been your first impressions of Thomas beforehand, if anything, and then kind of what kind of kind of stands out? >> Yeah, I was excited, man. I needed a Yale guy or somebody like Ivy League just to take some of the flack off the Notre Dame stuff. It's every day with these guys. Uh, and so that's one. I There's some family friends that knew him in the past and he's a he's a dog. He can move really well throughout, you know, before practices. Like he has incredible speed. He's kind of a freak athlete. Uh and yeah, he's in tune. He he knows ball. He's been around the game and played at a high level in this league. And so it's a huge addition to the room. He brings a lot of character, a lot of versatility to the to the unit. You >> mentioned you mentioned Nick there. How I mean, he did everything he did as a rookie role. How excited are you to see what he can do >> given another year and more time? >> I'm excited. Nick is one of one uh personalitywise, juice-wise, uh you know, having him as a rookie was really funny and maybe frustrating at times just because he's uh he has some swagger to him for sure. U and to see him become a leader uh is pretty cool. I mean, there's no, you know, I know he's not a he's out the rookie phase yet u three games. Uh but, you know, it's just fun to see him do his thing. I mean, he is so special. He's one of one in this league. You you could give him comparisons to a lot of different players, but he it's like nothing is what he does. Um and so if we can maximize him this year, I mean it's he is the heart of this thing. Uh in terms of just talent, uh he's he's really special. >> Three games into year two. >> Three games in year two. That's when you're not a rookie anymore. Yeah. >> I don't know. Uh I had a OG vet my rookie year. I said that. And so it's just been a thing. Uh a year and three games. >> You're three now. Mike McDonald defense, year three in this scheme. What's that next step now look like? Especially, you know, how quickly this off seasonason went and just trying to figure out where you can take this now. Yeah, it is shocking how much we have installed uh in the defense because Mike I think there's understanding that the guys are doing the extra work to kind of if who wasn't here last year the past few years to be at a certain level and everyone in here like okay we're not yeah you want to start at the at the ground floor but let's let's really get this thing going and so there's a little bit of that um but I say Mike's superpower is catering his plays and his scheme and our defense to the players. Like that's the everyone has the same plays really. Like it's how and why and when we execute them. Um that's that's what makes Mike special. And so he's been in the lab. We have some good stuff dialed up for sure and we will throughout the rest of the season. >> Off topic one. Uh in the NFL PA survey, you guys got several A grades. One of them was team travel. >> What do you think goes into getting an A for team travel? >> Yeah, that was that was definitely an intentional thing. Um that was been a really hot topic around here because Seahawks maybe not this year but on average usually travel just because we're further um we travel the most um you know year in year out. Uh and so it is really critical like that we can be prepared for a game if we're traveling east on those you know those 10 a.m. games for us. Um and I would say Sam Ramsey, Mike McDonald, several people high up have been really intentional about like the plan and execution. and we travel two days before. We got a bigger plane so guys cannot feel cramped and their legs can be fresh. Uh the hydration, the nutritionist, Andrea and Sammy do a great job. I mean sleep everything goes into account. They set up and tee us up so nice so that those East Coast games that our stats are really good, it's because we really work at it. Um it's all super intentional stuff. How important is Derek Hall to the defense? How excited are you to see sticking around for a few more years? >> Man, it's cool. It's really cool to see somebody, you know, be a rookie and then like get like that contract uh and become a leader and become a a force multiplier, and that's that's Dehaul. I think there's nobody that talks more or gets more talked that to uh than Derek. Um, everyone on his ass all the time. Uh, and at the same time, everyone is hugging him, dapping him up because it it's work. Like he he it's really special when somebody you you know they earned it. Uh it wasn't given, you know, there wasn't a draft status thing, clout, none of that. It's all work. Um and so yeah, he's uh he's special. Not person locker room doesn't love Deh Hall. Um you'll hear him. You probably can hear him right now if you listen uh closely. He's loud. Uh he's he's funny. Um, but he's a pro and he's definitely the epitome of Seahawk. >> Why do you think he attracts the the smack talk? >> He's the loudest one in the locker room. I mean, Spoon's a close second. I, you know, I rarely use it from time to time, but uh, man, now, man, I'm I'm older. I'm a little bit wiser. So, I bought some property this past offseason. Well, I guess this off seasonason back home. And now now the extension is in, starting to do house plans and, you know, want to want to do a family compound. So, that's my next step. >> What kind of boat did you get? >> Uh, I got a 239 QSFS. So, uh, my next step up is going to be the 291. Uh, which is pretty big. Probably probably next off seasonason. You know, I I won't have time to enjoy it before camp starts. So, probably next officer. Yeah, it's it's a center console. Uh built it out myself. Custom 300 Yamaha on the back. You You can't go to a boat dealer and find that motor. You got to order that one. So, it's pretty cool. >> Uh Jul, we were asking Julian about your style of play and the word he used to describe it was violent. There's different ways to play your position. Why do you think violence is? Why do you think that's your style of play? >> I think that's just who I am in my core. You know, I I feel like when I go out on the field every day, you know, even in practice right now, otaas, you kind of have to tame and take care of each other and take care of the way you practice. But, you know, my goal is to displace you and get to the ball. And, you know, I think that's that's what we eat, think, or breathe on defensive side of the ball. There's no man between you and the ball at all times. And whether that be run or pass, you know, obviously I'm I'm working different things in my pass rush this offseason to really enhance my game, but you can know power is coming. You can't stop it. And I think that's just the mentality that I have, man. And I think it really stems from growing up and everything that I went through, man. I just I hit stuff head on. I go straight through the process and there's nothing that's going to stop me. >> Kind of touching on that, you know, your story when drafting was a pretty big milestone for you to kind of get this contract to come into after all of that. Kind of what that kind of your family was here for. >> Yeah, it was it was special. I think number one, again, sharing that moment with my mom and uh you know, my sister and then my agents, man, just the countless hours that they put in over the past few weeks staying up late because they live on the East Coast. So, by the time I get out the building here and get home and get settled, it's pretty late there. But, you know, them taking the time and, you know, getting this thing worked out. But, I mean, it's pretty special. Looking from where I come from to look at where the Lord has blessed me now, man, it's it's unbelievable. It's unimaginable. And just continue to show people, man. You know, no matter where you start, no matter where you come from, there's always hope. And, you know, I'm I'm big. I'm big in my faith, obviously. So, I'm I'm faith based. But, I mean, just believe in God, man. There's sky's the limit. >> The the performance you had in the Super Bowl with the sack sack and the of course humble and everything. I I guess how much did that kind of mean to you and and you know what what really went right in that game previously? >> Yeah, so I mean I last year was pretty tough for me. I mean obviously you know the passion rate was high, the pressure rate was high but it it was hard for me to get home and um you know I just always I'm like God like I'm there. I'm there. I'm there. And man, I I was letting it worry me so much and one night I just prayed. I'm like Lord whenever the time comes I'll be here. I'll be prepared. I'm going just continue to do the work, continue to grind every day and put my best foot forward. And what better time for it to show itself uh on the worldwide stage, man, the Super Bowl. And I was just overjoyed, you know, I I was so overjoyed for that moment, you know, knowing all the work that I put in all year and have it show up at that time. It was pretty special for me. >> You guys talk in that locker room about not chasing stats, playing the right way. Uh what does it mean to then be rewarded for playing that way, even necessarily without having the the big numbers? >> Yeah, I think it's huge. Um, just again speaking back on the aspect of how they view me upstairs. You know, I think that's huge and you know, I love Mike and his staff and I know they feel the same way about me and I think that show obviously over the last couple days of what they've done, you know, for me and my family moving forward and man, I think it's huge and again, bro, it's just the tip of the iceberg. There's there's so much more for me and I know there's so much greater heights that I can go to in my game of ball and it just continue to work towards that every single day. >> What What do those greater heights What do those greater heights look like for you as a player? What is that next step as far as, you know, now that you got this new contract going into year four? What are those areas where you're like, I've still got a lot higher to go in terms of get my seal? >> Mainly, man, just detailing out my game, detailing out my pass rush, you know, you know, like again, power is my thing. I feel like I set the edge. I play the run really well, but man, just being able to get back out on edges, you know, being able to set up my rushes a lot better and turn those pressures and hits that I had last year in the sacks and getting there just that much of a tick faster. And I think we're drilling that every single day. And that's what I'm working. I haven't worked any power. Um, and that's that's just what it is for me, man. I'm just trying to put the nail on the hammer, you know, keep pushing envelope and continue to grow in areas where I feel like I need to grow. >> You learned so much last year from Demarcus Lawrence. Now you've got Dante Fowler here. Much a different style player. How much does that benefit you now to have another veteran that plays different stylistically to help enhance your game? >> Huge. Huge. Uh, Tay came in and I introduced myself and he was like, "Hey man, I'm glad to be here. you know, I'm happy to help in any way that I can. And every single day, again, we talk a lot of crap to each other, but we go out there and we push each other, you know, just speaking the aspect of the day, we were working something and it was kind of I really couldn't wrap my head around it. He really slowed down and just helped show me the way and how he would play it. And I I mean, everybody know he's a speed rusher. So, been able to have two different aspect of DAW who's crazy and insane and does all the right things and then having someone who's been here just as long, but the speed dynamic is out of this world. I mean, that's what he's known for. And be able to have both of those guys and continue to lean on them, I think is huge for me in my development. >> Appreciate it. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

title: Cam Heyward Media Availability (June 3) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Nick Saban said yesterday, "Not all change is bad." TBD. I don't I don't want to answer that. I think I think uh there's just a lot that um we're still absorbing. Um you know, it's not like there's going to be one good coach in the league and you know, always admired coach McCarthy from afar and just want to learn. I think that's the the easiest thing you can do is put your ego aside and just learn from you know great coaches. >> They put another year on your contract. How difficult is it to keep maintaining your ability to play at the level you're at? Does it get more difficult each year? >> Yeah, but that's the challenge you live up to. I mean out here just on the field, have you had that moment where you're like you're expecting to hear his voice or just seeing him out here? you know we used to park next to each other every day. Yes, check it out if you can. >> [laughter] >> After being he talked about always getting calls to come back. What is your take? >> I would say that but it's like the Rams already stacked on D line. Who's who who's going to bounce to the side but yeah we'll see. It's not like he's any short of talented or ready for that moment. Dude works out every single day. So you know good luck to the NFC. >> What's been your impression of coach Brandon and not just like his schematics or anything like that but also the way he handles >> He's a very attention to detailed you know he's throwing a lot at our guys and seeing how well we absorb it but I think he's open to communication as well. You know, I think from last year left a bitter taste in our mouth. But then you add guys like Jamal Dean, Jaquan Brisker, Sebastian Joseph Day. I think it just it's a multitude of that and then our younger guys continue to grow, which benefits us and you know, hopefully our older guys are still on the cusp of getting better. >> Have you done any 90s, early 2000s hip hop reports for Patrick Graham? >> No, because I lived in the 90s. >> But no, I like I like screwing with Jack because Jack had to present on um Goodie Mob and I think Tribe uh Tribe Called Quest uh But it's funny because you can tell they're just reading off of Wikipedia. >> I'm like, you're not really listening to that. So >> Cam, your perspective on Aaron Rodgers Roman Empire today, 60 yards showing. >> It's what he's supposed to do. >> 42 years >> So, it's just a number. There's been other quarterbacks that have been able to do it. I've been told he's one of the best that's ever done it. He's going to keep proving it.
